title: Senior's toolkit: running containers
summary: The run, ps, logs, exec and inspect flags you use every day to start a container and see what it is doing.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: running containers
steps.body: Start it, see it, read its logs, step inside, ask Docker what it knows. Most container work is these six commands with the right flags.

toolkit.what: Starts a container in the background with a name, a published port and configuration from the environment.
flags: a name to use instead of the id
set environment variables, one by one or from a file

toolkit.what: A throwaway interactive container: try a command in a clean image, then it disappears.
flags: delete the container when it exits
override an image whose entrypoint is not a shell

toolkit.what: Lists containers, including the ones that already exited. The status shows the exit code.
Reads what the app wrote to stdout and stderr. The first stop when a container misbehaves.
flags: only the last 10 minutes (or a timestamp)

toolkit.what: Opens a shell inside a running container to check files, environment and the network from its point of view.
flags: run as root (when the image runs as a normal user)
set a variable for this command only
toolkit.when: the container runs but behaves oddly

toolkit.what: Asks Docker for one fact about a container: exit code, OOM kill, IP, mounts, restart count.
flags: a Go template that picks fields
true if the kernel killed it for memory
the environment it was started with

toolkit.what: Copies a file out of (or into) a container, even a stopped one.

steps.prompt: Match each flag to what it does.
pairs: delete the container when it exits
publish container port 80 on host port 8080
only lines from the last ten minutes
run an interactive command inside a running container

steps.prompt: You ran `docker run -d --name api myorg/api:1.4.0`. `docker ps` shows nothing. What do you run first?
options: `docker ps -a` to see its status and exit code, then `docker logs api`
steps.explain: `docker ps` hides stopped containers. `ps -a` shows `Exited (1)`, and `docker logs` works on stopped containers, so you see the error it printed. `exec` needs a running container.

steps.prompt: Follow the last 100 log lines of `api` from the past 15 minutes.
steps.explain: `-f` follows, `--since` limits by time, `--tail` limits by count. `--until` exists too, for a window in the past; there is no `--head`.

steps.prompt: The app inside `api` listens on port 8080. You started it with `docker run -d -p 80:8080 api-img`. From the host, which URL reaches it?
steps.explain: `-p host:container`: the left number is on your machine, the right one inside the container. `api` as a host name only works between containers on a user-defined network.

steps.prompt: Which commands work on a container that has already exited?

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: When a container misbehaves, go in the same order every time: `docker ps -a`, `docker logs --since`, `docker inspect -f`, and only then `docker exec`. Use `--rm` for every throwaway container so your machine does not fill with dead ones.
